_readme: Drop a new option folder (with spec.json + model) inside its category folder, then add the folder name to that category's options list below. Nothing in index.html / main.css / main.js needs to change.

instructor.text: Welcome to the Thermal Management lab. Every motor and ESC dissipates I²R heat — here you will measure how hot they run, how fast they get there, and how to cool them so they survive.

Start in Input Parameters — tap any component tile to open its option library, then use the new Environment & Cooling card to set ambient temperature, airflow and Static/Forward flight mode. Everything here is a live control — nothing runs automatically.

Module 1 · Steady-State Temp Sweep: pick a throttle, press Arm, let it settle, then press Record Point. Repeat at five different throttle settings — the T_ss vs I² chart should trace a straight line whose slope is R_m·R_th.

Module 1 · Thermal Time Constant: arm the bench and watch the heating curve climb. Drag the τ-cursor on the chart to the knee where it reaches 63.2% of its rise — that time is τ. Try a second throttle: τ should read the same, because it depends only on R_th·C_th, not on load.

Module 2 · ESC Thermal Check: run full throttle and watch the ESC gauge against the 80 °C limit. If it trips into the red, drag a Heatsink onto the ESC or pick a beefier ESC tile to bring it back under the line.

Module 3 · Rotor-Wash Cooling: in still air the case can run dangerously hot. Raise the cooling-airflow slider, drag the Ducted Fan onto the motor, and switch Static → Forward — watch the required-cooling bar and the settled temperature fall as coverage improves.
Outstanding — every experiment is complete. Thermal Pads + Heatsink are now unlocked in the Outputs panel.

reward.name: Thermal Pads + Heatsink
reward.desc: Unlocked build reward — a finned aluminium heatsink and conductive thermal pad kit for motor/ESC cooling. Drop reward.glb in assets/reward/ to display a real model here.
